messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 1769004321 - sustained p99 latency increase and connection queue growth on /v1/chat.stream (hosted). Queue depth up ~3x in 3m. See: https://metrics.redwood.internal/alerts/1769004321

ryan: paging SRE oncall — @maya are you available?

maya: taking this. seeing p99 jump from ~110ms to ~2.1s, grpc waiter count climbing. KV cache miss rate spiking. grabbing the live dashboards.

jamie: I can pull runtime traces and check batching locks. streaming sockets seem to be accumulating blocked writers.

maya: quick options: disable streaming at edge for affected route, apply temporary per-tenant concurrency caps, or shift new sessions to non-streaming fallback. Fastest is edge toggle + caps.

alex: product note — disabling streaming will change UX for anyone relying on incremental tokens. Need short customer notify. Any enterprise impact?

leah: support: current active streaming customers = 7, two are latency-sensitive trading testers (high priority). I'll prep banner text and canned replies.

ryan: handing mitigation to maya. I'll stay on the line.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) flip feature flag for hosted chat.stream to disable streaming responses 2) reduce per-tenant concurrency for free tier from 25 -> 8 3) apply gentle connection shaping (10%) for new streaming session accepts. Hold for 10m and reassess.

maya: executing commands now:
```
# feature flag toggle (prod)
ffctl set hosted.chat_stream.streaming_enabled false --env=prod --author=maya
# apply concurrency cap
quotactl set --env=prod --tier=free --concurrency=8 --reason="incident 1769004321"
# connection shaping
netctl shape --env=prod --scope=hosted --policy=accept_rate:0.9
```

incident-bot: action recorded: ff-20260301-1769 by maya

maya: also pushed a more aggressive upstream keepalive for streaming sockets (idle 30s) to help clear zombied connections.

maya: toggle ran at 1769004378. running quick smoke against non-customer tokens.

jamie: watching traces — pre-toggle backlog ~740, immediate post-toggle backlog ~110. p99 back down to ~300ms in the affected pool.

maya: smoke checks OK. text-only fallback path returning full responses, no errors seen in logs. KV miss rate reduced but still slightly elevated.

ryan: good. Jamie please keep an eye on runtime traces for any unexpected errors; Leah finalize and post the customer banner.

leah: banner drafted: "Temporary change: Streaming responses are disabled for the hosted chat API to stabilize latency. Responses will still be delivered in full; expected time window ~10-30 minutes. We'll update here when streaming is restored." Posting now.

alex: flagged two trading testers for direct AM outreach — cc @olivia. Sales/AMs notified.

maya: added short-term quota holds for those two tenants and emailed AMs.

jamie: telemetry update link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/streaming/1769004385 — overall p99 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~310ms. backlog decreased significantly.

maya: setting 10m observation timer. Criteria to restore: p99 < 500ms AND grpc backlog < 200 for 10m straight.

incident-bot: incident status changed to mitigated->monitoring. incident_id=INC-20260301-17

ryan: great work. Maya add the exact commands and timestamps to the runbook. We'll follow up with a postmortem and action items (KV cache investigation, batching lock analysis, streaming backpressure improvements).

maya: follow-ups assigned:
- eng-runtime: investigate continuous-batching contention under high connection churn (assigned to srinivas)
- eng-ml: analyze model-side kv cache thrash pattern
- infra: add more granular tracing for streaming socket lifecycle

leah: customer banner posted. reactions: :bell: :thumbsup:

maya: handing off monitoring to night oncall @lucy at 1769004587. leaving runbook notes and play commands.

lucy: ack. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if thresholds breach. :eyes:
notes: mitigation: streaming disabled for hosted chat.stream; per-tenant concurrency caps applied; connection shaping and keepalive tightened. smoke test passed; monitoring criteria set for re-enable. runbook entries updated.
